replies.name: Rory Watts
replies.text: @danshipper I was finally able to fully migrate off codex-cli because of this. Was still sending messages between tmux-sessions but now that's solved!

replies.name: The Data Nerd
replies.text: @danshipper the self-organizing threads are nice-to-have. the worktree-per-task bit is the actual unlock - you stop being the single-threaded scheduler standing in front of the agent.

replies.name: Darshan Yadav
replies.text: @danshipper Codex orchestrating its own worktrees changes the mental model from 'IDE tool' to 'autonomous system with persistent state.' The question becomes: who reviews what Codex decides to pin vs discard? That's the governance layer nobody is building yet.

replies.name: Global Perspective 🌐
replies.text: @danshipper We're slowly replacing task management with delegation management.

replies.name: Umer Farooq
replies.text: @danshipper Damn that's brutal. Being sick is the absolute worst, hope you're taking it easy.

replies.name: Alex Zh
replies.text: @danshipper would have been nice if they reset weekly limits too, i gotta wait till tomorrow or melt api budget 😭

replies.name: Edgar Cerecerez

replies.name: Ahmer Sultan
replies.text:
@danshipper I hear, more cognitive load in the guise of productivity. 

Probably the limit is my own self, I’m unable to let codex or cursor take full control. 🤫🤷

replies.name: sofiane
replies.text: @danshipper the gui is no longer a constraint. i increasingly see this new ux pattern emerging. as long as the background cli can handle what the model is throwing at it, personalized software is finally becoming a reality, a pleasant one.
